questions.scenario: An agent can issue refunds. A person must decide before any refund is sent.
questions.question: What should you configure?

options.why: It does not add approval.

options.text: A second deployment of the same model
options.why: It does not pause the run.

options.text: Require approval on the issue_refund tool
options.why: Correct. The run pauses until a decision is returned.

options.text: A lower temperature for the model
options.why: Temperature does not control approval.

questions.explanation: Approval modes pause tool calls until a person decides.

questions.scenario: Policy states a refund above ₹20,000 must never be issued by the agent, whatever a reviewer says.
questions.question: Where should you enforce the limit?

options.why: A model can ignore or misread instructions.
It does not apply business rules.
Monitoring does not enforce limits.

options.text: In the tool code, as a rule that rejects larger amounts
options.why: Correct. Code enforces the limit regardless of the model or the approver.

questions.explanation: Use code for absolute limits and approvals for judgement calls.

questions.scenario: An auditor asks who approved a refund and when.
questions.question: What should have been captured?

options.text: The tool call and the approval decision in the trace
options.why: Correct. Traces provide the audit record.
It does not show who approved.
It is unrelated to approval.
It does not relate to approvals.

questions.explanation: Record tool calls and decisions so that actions can be audited.

questions.scenario: An agent has two tools: lookup_order, which reads data, and issue_refund, which moves money.
questions.question: Which tools should normally require approval?

options.why: Money movement should be reviewed.
Correct. Write actions with financial impact carry the risk.
The read-only tool carries less risk.
Approving every read adds friction without equal risk reduction.

questions.explanation: Apply approval where impact is high and keep low-risk reads smooth.

questions.scenario: A run is paused with a pending approval request.
questions.question: What must the application do to continue the run?

options.why: It does not answer the request.

options.text: Restart the application and hope the tool runs
options.why: The decision is still required.

options.text: Return an approval response that approves or rejects the request
options.why: Correct. The run resumes after a decision.
It would discard the run.

questions.explanation: Approval requests are answered with a decision, then the run resumes.
